hints: Look at the exact conditions in each statement, Group 17 chemistry often changes completely with cold versus hot or dilute versus concentrated.
Recall that reducing power increases down the group, so iodide is the strongest reducing agent and sulfuric acid is a strong oxidising acid.
Check the trends for hydrogen halide bond strength and for silver halide solubility in ammonia to eliminate the other three statements.
walkthrough:
**Recall chlorine with NaOH**

Think of this as a disproportionation reaction where chlorine is both oxidised and reduced. The product depends on temperature.

Cold dilute $\text{NaOH}$: $\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Hot concentrated $\text{NaOH}$: $3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

**Compare HCl and HBr stability**

Thermal stability depends on bond strength. A smaller halogen gives better overlap and a stronger, harder to break $\text{H-X}$ bond.

Bond strength: $\text{H-Cl} > \text{H-Br}$, so $\text{HCl}$ is more stable. This is linked to chlorine being smaller and more electronegative than bromine, not less.

**Test iodide with concentrated sulfuric acid**

Down Group 17, halide ions become stronger reducing agents: $\text{Cl}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{I}^-$.

Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is an oxidising acid and $\text{I}^-$ is strong enough to reduce it, itself being oxidised:
$$2\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 2e^-$$

**Recall silver halides in ammonia**

Silver chloride dissolves in dilute ammonia, silver bromide needs concentrated ammonia, but silver iodide is insoluble even in concentrated ammonia. So the solubility trend decreases down the group.

options.A: Incorrect. Cold dilute NaOH gives NaCl and NaClO (sodium chlorate(I)), while hot concentrated NaOH gives NaCl and NaClO3. The statement mixes cold with concentrated, so the conditions and products do not match.
options.B: Incorrect. It is true that HCl is more thermally stable than HBr because the H-Cl bond is stronger and shorter, but the reason given is backwards. Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine, not less.
options.C: Correct. Iodide is a powerful reducing agent and concentrated sulfuric acid is a powerful oxidising agent. Iodide reduces the acid (to SO2, S or H2S) while being oxidised to brown iodine, I2. This is why HI cannot be prepared using concentrated sulfuric acid.
options.D: Incorrect. AgCl is soluble in dilute aqueous ammonia, AgBr is only soluble in concentrated ammonia, and AgI is insoluble even in concentrated ammonia. Students often confuse the trend and think all silver halides dissolve.
